title: Spelling -able & -ible
keyIdea: The endings -able and -ible sound the same, so test the root instead. If a whole word is left when you cover the ending, it is usually -able (enjoyable, dependable). If not, it is usually -ible (visible, possible). A related word ending in -ation also points to -able (adoration, adorable). At the join, most roots drop a final e (adorable), roots ending in soft ce or ge keep it (noticeable, changeable), and y after a consonant turns to i (reliable). For adverbs, swap the final e for y: comfortably, possibly. Some words break the guide, such as sensible, so check a dictionary when unsure.
familyTip: When your child meets a word ending in -able or -ible, ask them to cover the ending with a finger. Is a real word left? Enjoy is, so enjoyable. Vis is not, so visible. Then hunt for the rule breakers together: sensible, flexible and capable are good ones to know by heart.

visual.caption: Which ending? Drag each root, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: test the root, drag on an ending, fix the join, use -ation clues, make -ably and -ibly adverbs, and sort the rule breakers.

kid: Say enjoyable and visible. The endings sound the same. So you cannot spell them by sound alone.
Try the root test. Cover the ending with your finger. Enjoy is a real word, so it is enjoyable. Vis is not a word, so it is visible.
Watch the join. Adore drops its e: adorable. Notice keeps its e, so the c still says s: noticeable. Rely changes y to i: reliable.
To say how something is done, swap the last e for y. Comfortable becomes comfortably. Possible becomes possibly. Be careful: possiblely is wrong.
adult: Ages 9 to 10. The National Curriculum in England lists words ending in -able and -ible, and -ably and -ibly, in English Appendix 1 for Years 5 and 6. The endings sound alike because the vowel is unstressed, so spelling needs a strategy.

The guide. -able is far more common. It is used when a complete root word can be heard (dependable, comfortable, reliable) and when there is a related word ending in -ation (adorable, applicable, tolerable). -ible is common when no complete root can be heard (possible, horrible, terrible). Roots ending in ce or ge keep the e before -able so the c or g stays soft (noticeable, changeable); forcible and legible use -ible instead.

Common mistakes. Children spell by ear and pick the wrong ending (horrable, dependible). They drop the e after a soft c or g (noticable) or keep it when it should go (adoreable). For adverbs they add -ly to the whole word (possiblely) instead of changing e to y. Words such as sensible, flexible, accessible, capable and probable break the guide and must be learned.

In the lab your child tests eight roots and spells six words by dragging an ending on. They fix the join for six roots and choose a or i for six words using -ation clues and soft c or g. They make five adverbs and sort eight words into follows the guide or rule breaker.

practice.hint: Cover the ending. Is depend a whole word?
practice.explain: Depend is a whole word, so it takes -able: dependable.

practice.prompt: A word ending in -able has {n} letters. How many letters does its -ably adverb have?
practice.hint: Does the adverb add letters, or swap one?
practice.explain: The final e swaps for y (comfortable → comfortably), so the adverb still has {n} letters.

practice.prompt: Pick the correct spelling of the word that means easy to see.
practice.hint: Is vis a word on its own?
practice.explain: Vis is not a whole word, so the ending is -ible: visible.

practice.prompt: A root word has {n} letters and ends in e, like adore. You drop the e and add -able. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: Take one letter away, then add the four letters of able.
practice.explain: Dropping the e leaves {=n-1} letters, and able adds 4, so the word has {=n+3} letters (adore 5 → adorable 8).

practice.hint: Does the adverb add -ly, or swap the last letter?
practice.explain: Terrible becomes terribly: the e changes to y. Adding -ly to the whole word gives the wrong spelling terriblely.

pool.prompt: Which spelling of notice + able is correct?
pool.hint: What sound should the c keep?
pool.explain: Keep the e so the c stays soft (like s). Without it, c before a would sound hard, like cap.

pool.prompt: Which spelling of rely + able is correct?
pool.hint: What happens to a y after a consonant?
pool.explain: A y after a consonant turns to i before the ending: reli + able = reliable.

pool.prompt: Adoration ends in -ation. Which is the matching adjective?
pool.hint: An -ation cousin points to one ending. What happens to the e?
pool.explain: A related -ation word points to -able, and adore drops its e: adorable.

pool.prompt: Which word breaks the root-word guide?
pool.hint: Which has a whole root word but still takes -ible?
pool.explain: Sense is a whole word, yet sensible takes -ible. Enjoyable and horrible both follow the guide.

pool.prompt: Turn possible into an adverb. Which spelling is right?
pool.explain: Possible becomes possibly: the final e changes to y. Nothing is added.

pool.prompt: A root word has {n} letters and ends in ce or ge, like notice. How many letters does its -able word have?
pool.hint: Is the e kept or dropped after a soft c or g?
pool.explain: The e stays to keep the c or g soft, so all {n} letters stay and able adds 4: {=n+4} letters (notice 6 → noticeable 10).

pool.prompt: A root word has {n} letters and ends in a consonant then y, like rely. How many letters does its -able word have?
pool.hint: The y changes to i. Does that change the count?
pool.explain: The y swaps for i, so the root keeps {n} letters, and able adds 4: {=n+4} letters (rely 4 → reliable 8).

pool.prompt: Why can't you choose between -able and -ible by sound?
choices: The endings sound the same when you say them.
-able is only used in long words.
pool.hint: Say comfortable and horrible. Listen to the endings.
pool.explain: The vowel in the ending is unstressed, so -able and -ible sound alike. That is why you test the root instead.

pool.prompt: Which spelling of the word meaning safe to eat is correct?
pool.hint: Is ed a whole word with this meaning?
pool.explain: There is no whole root word in edible, so it takes -ible.
